html:
The Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma is one of two nations of the Iowa, or Ioway, people. Its land lies near Perkins in central Oklahoma. The map shows it in 1492, but the Iowa only came there in the 1880s.

In 1492 the ancestors of the Iowa lived further northeast, in the upper Mississippi valley, and were likely part of the Oneota culture. They spoke Chiwere, a Siouan language shared with the Otoe and close to that of the Ho-Chunk. They farmed maize and hunted bison, and the state of Iowa is named after them.

Treaties in the 1800s took their land. In 1836 they moved to a reservation on the Kansas and Nebraska border. Some families went south to Indian Territory, where a reservation was set up for them in 1883, later broken into private plots.
